verses.zh: 以利沙曾对所救活之子的那妇人说：「你和你的全家要起身往你可住的地方去住，因为耶和华命饥荒降在这地七年。」
verses.en: Now Elisha advised the woman whose son he had brought back to life, “You and your family should go and live somewhere else for a while,[NOTE:1] for the Lord has decreed that a famine will overtake the land for seven years.”
notes: Heb “Get up and go, you and your house, and live temporarily where you can live temporarily.”

verses.zh: 妇人就起身，照神人的话带着全家往非利士地去，住了七年。
verses.en: So the woman did as the prophet said.[NOTE:1] She and her family went and lived in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
notes: Heb “and the woman got up and did according to the word of the man of God.”

verses.zh: 七年完了，那妇人从非利士地回来，就出去为自己的房屋田地哀告王。
verses.en: After seven years the woman returned from the land of the Philistines and went to ask the king to give her back her house and field.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and went out to cry out to the king for her house and her field.”

verses.zh: 那时王正与神人的仆人基哈西说：「请你将以利沙所行的一切大事告诉我。」
verses.en: Now the king was talking to Gehazi, the prophet’s[NOTE:1] servant, and said, “Tell me all the great things that Elisha has done.”
notes: Heb “man of God’s.”

verses.zh: 基哈西告诉王以利沙如何使死人复活，恰巧以利沙所救活、她儿子的那妇人为自己的房屋田地来哀告王。基哈西说：「我主我王，这就是那妇人，这是她的儿子，就是以利沙所救活的。」
verses.en: While Gehazi[NOTE:1] was telling the king how Elisha[NOTE:2] had brought the dead back to life, the woman whose son he had brought back to life came to ask the king for her house and field.[NOTE:3] Gehazi said, “My master, O king, this is the very woman, and this is her son whom Elisha brought back to life!”
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Gehazi) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Heb “and look, the woman whose son he had brought back to life was crying out to the king for her house and her field.”sn The legal background of the situation is uncertain. For a discussion of possibilities, see M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 87-88.

verses.zh: 王问那妇人，她就把那事告诉王。于是王为她派一个太监，说：「凡属这妇人的都还给她，自从她离开本地直到今日，她田地的出产也都还给她。」
verses.en: The king asked the woman about it, and she gave him the details.[NOTE:1] The king assigned a eunuch to take care of her request and ordered him,[NOTE:2] “Give her back everything she owns, as well as the amount of crops her field produced from the day she left the land until now.”
notes: Heb “and the king asked the woman and she told him.”
Heb “and he assigned to her an official, saying.”

verses.zh: 以利沙来到大马士革，亚兰王便・哈达正患病。有人告诉王说：「神人来到这里了。」
verses.en: Elisha traveled to Damascus while King Ben Hadad of Syria was sick. The king[NOTE:1] was told, “The prophet[NOTE:2] has come here.”
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “man of God” (also a second time in this verse and in v. 11).

verses.zh: 王就吩咐哈薛说：「你带着礼物去见神人，托他求问耶和华，我这病能好不能好？」
verses.en: So the king told Hazael, “Take a gift[NOTE:1] and go visit the prophet. Request from him an oracle from the Lord. Ask him,[NOTE:2] ‘Will I recover from this sickness?’”
notes: The Hebrew text also has “in your hand.”
Heb “Inquire of the Lord through him, saying.”

verses.zh: 于是哈薛用四十个骆驼，驮着大马士革的各样美物为礼物，去见以利沙。到了他那里，站在他面前，说：「你儿子亚兰王便．哈达打发我来见你，他问说：『我这病能好不能好？』」
verses.en: So Hazael went to visit Elisha.[NOTE:1] He took along a gift,[NOTE:2] as well as[NOTE:3] 40 camel-loads of all the fine things of Damascus. When he arrived, he stood before him and said, “Your son,[NOTE:4] King Ben Hadad of Syria, has sent me to you with this question,[NOTE:5] ‘Will I recover from this sickness?’”
notes: Heb “him”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The Hebrew text also has “in his hand.”

Heb “and.” It is possible that the conjunction is here explanatory, equivalent to English “that is.” In this case the 40 camel-loads constitute the “gift” and one should translate, “He took along a gift, consisting of 40 camel-loads of all the fine things of Damascus.”
The words “your son” emphasize the king’s respect for the prophet.
Heb “saying.”

verses.zh: 以利沙对哈薛说：「你回去告诉他说，这病必能好；但耶和华指示我，他必要死。」
verses.en: Elisha said to him, “Go and tell him, ‘You will surely recover,’[NOTE:1] but the Lord has revealed to me that he will surely die.”
notes: The consonantal text (Kethib) reads, “Go, say, ‘Surely you will not (לֹא, loʾ) live.’” In this case the vav beginning the next clause could be translated “for” or “because.” The reading tradition (Qere) has, “Go, say to him (לוֹ, lo), ‘You will surely recover.’” In this case the vav (ו) beginning the next clause would be translated “although” or “but.” The Qere has the support of some medieval Hebrew mss and the ancient versions, and is consistent with v. 14, where Hazael tells the king, “You will surely recover.” It also fits the immediate context. The sentence “you will live,” to be told to Ben Hadad and meaning to recover from the sickness contrasts telling Hazael that Ben Hadad will die. The missing component is the means of Ban Hadad’s death. So Elisha looks at Hazael until he is embarrassed because as a prophet he knows that Hazael will kill Ben Hadad (not the sickness). It is possible that a scribe has changed לוֹ, “to him,” to לֹא, “not,” because he felt that Elisha would not lie to the king. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 90. But it is possible that Hazael, once he found out he would become the next king, decided to lie to the king to facilitate his assassination plot by making the king feel secure.

verses.zh: 神人定睛看着哈薛，甚至他惭愧。神人就哭了；
verses.en: Elisha[NOTE:1] just stared at him until Hazael became uncomfortable.[NOTE:2] Then the prophet started crying.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and he made his face stand [i.e., be motionless] and set [his face?] until embarrassment.”

verses.zh: 哈薛说：「我主为甚么哭？」回答说：「因为我知道你必苦害以色列人，用火焚烧他们的保障，用刀杀死他们的壮丁，摔死他们的婴孩，剖开他们的孕妇。」
verses.en: Hazael asked, “Why are you crying, my master?” He replied, “Because I know the trouble you will cause the Israelites. You will set fire to their fortresses, kill their young men with the sword, smash their children to bits, and rip open their pregnant women.”

verses.zh: 哈薛说：「你仆人算甚么，不过是一条狗，焉能行这大事呢？」以利沙回答说：「耶和华指示我，你必作亚兰王。」
verses.en: Hazael said, “How could your servant, who is as insignificant as a dog, accomplish this great military victory?”[NOTE:1] Elisha answered, “The Lord has revealed to me that you will be the king of Syria.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Indeed, what is your servant, a dog, that he could do this great thing?” With his reference to a dog, Hazael is not denying that he is a “dog” and protesting that he would never commit such a dastardly “dog-like” deed. Rather, as Elisha’s response indicates, Hazael is suggesting that he, like a dog, is too insignificant to ever be in a position to lead such conquests.
Heb “The Lord has shown me you [as] king over Syria.”

verses.zh: 哈薛离开以利沙，回去见他的主人。主人问他说：「以利沙对你说甚么？」回答说：「他告诉我你必能好。」
verses.en: He left Elisha and went to his master. Ben Hadad[NOTE:1] asked him, “What did Elisha tell you?” Hazael[NOTE:2] replied, “He told me you would surely recover.”
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Ben Hadad) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “he”; the referent (Hazael) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 次日，哈薛拿被窝浸在水中，蒙住王的脸，王就死了。于是哈薛篡了他的位。
verses.en: The next day Hazael[NOTE:1] took a piece of cloth, dipped it in water, and spread it over Ben Hadad’s[NOTE:2] face until he died. Then Hazael replaced him as king.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Hazael) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “his”; the referent (Ben Hadad) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 以色列王亚哈的儿子约兰第五年，犹大王约沙法还在位的时候，约沙法的儿子约兰登基作了犹大王。
verses.en: In the fifth year of the reign of Israel’s King Joram, son of Ahab, Jehoshaphat’s son Jehoram became king over Judah.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew text reads, “and in the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, and [or, ‘while’?] Jehoshaphat [was?] king of Judah, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah became king.” The first reference to “Jehoshaphat king of Judah” is probably due to a scribe accidentally copying the phrase from later in the verse. If the Hebrew text is retained, the verse probably refers to the beginning of a coregency between Jehoshaphat and Jehoram.

verses.zh: 约兰登基的时候年三十二岁，在耶路撒冷作王八年。
verses.en: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned for eight years in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 他行以色列诸王所行的，与亚哈家一样；因为他娶了亚哈的女儿为妻，行耶和华眼中看为恶的事。
verses.en: He followed in the footsteps of the kings of Israel, just as Ahab’s dynasty had done, for he married Ahab’s daughter.[NOTE:1] He did evil in the sight of[NOTE:2] the Lord.
notes: Heb “he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab did, for the daughter of Ahab was his wife.”
Heb “in the eyes of.”

verses.zh: 耶和华却因他仆人大卫的缘故，仍不肯灭绝犹大，照他所应许大卫的话，永远赐灯光与他的子孙。
verses.en: But the Lord was unwilling to destroy Judah. He preserved Judah for the sake of[NOTE:1] his servant David to whom he had promised a perpetual dynasty.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew has only one sentence, “and the Lord was unwilling to destroy Judah for the sake of.” The translation divides it for the sake of clarity.
Heb “just as he had said to him, to give to him a lamp for his sons all the days.” The metaphorical “lamp” symbolizes the Davidic dynasty; this is reflected in the translation.

verses.zh: 约兰年间，以东人背叛犹大，脱离他的权下，自己立王。
verses.en: During his reign Edom freed themselves from Judah’s control and set up their own king.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “in his days Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah and enthroned a king over them.”

verses.zh: 约兰率领所有的战车往撒益去，夜间起来，攻打围困他的以东人和车兵长；犹大兵就逃跑，各回各家去了。
verses.en: Jehoram[NOTE:1] crossed over to Zair with all his chariots. The Edomites, who had surrounded him, attacked at night and defeated him and his chariot officers.[NOTE:2] The Israelite army retreated to their homeland.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Joram,” which is a short form of the name Jehoram (also in vv. 23, 24).

Heb “and he arose at night and defeated Edom, who had surrounded him, and the chariot officers.” The Hebrew text as it stands gives the impression that Jehoram was surrounded and launched a victorious night counterattack. It would then be quite natural to understand the last statement in the verse to refer to an Edomite retreat. Yet v. 22 goes on to state that the Edomite revolt was successful. Therefore, if the MT is retained, it may be better to understand the final statement in v. 21 as a reference to an Israelite retreat (made in spite of the success described in the preceding sentence). Instead the translation assumes an emendation of the Hebrew text, adding a vav (ו) to the accusative sign before Edom, reading אֹתוֹ (ʾoto, “him,”) instead of just אֶת (ʾet). In this reading, Edom is the subject of the verb rather than the direct object, “Edom struck him.” This is more consistent with the context but there is no manuscript evidence in favor of this.
Heb “and the people fled to their tents.”

verses.zh: 这样，以东人背叛犹大，脱离他的权下，直到今日。那时立拿人也背叛了。
verses.en: So Edom has remained free from Judah’s control to this very day.[NOTE:1] At that same time Libnah also rebelled.
notes: Heb “and Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah until this day.”

verses.zh: 约兰其余的事，凡他所行的，都写在犹大列王记上。
verses.en: The rest of the events of Jehoram’s reign, including a record of his accomplishments, are recorded in the scroll called the Annals of the Kings of Judah.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “As for the rest of the acts of Joram and all which he did, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?”

verses.zh: 约兰与他列祖同睡，葬在大卫城他列祖的坟地里。他儿子亚哈谢接续他作王。
verses.en: Jehoram passed away[NOTE:1] and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Ahaziah replaced him as king.
notes: Heb “lay down with his fathers.”

verses.zh: 以色列王亚哈的儿子约兰十二年，犹大王约兰的儿子亚哈谢登基。
verses.en: In the twelfth year of the reign of Israel’s King Joram, son of Ahab, Jehoram’s son Ahaziah became king over Judah.

verses.zh: 他登基的时候年二十二岁，在耶路撒冷作王一年。他母亲名叫亚她利雅，是以色列王暗利的孙女。
verses.en: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned for one year in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1] His mother was Athaliah, the granddaughter[NOTE:2] of King Omri of Israel.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Hebrew בַּת (bat), “daughter,” can refer, as here to a granddaughter. See HALOT 166 s.v. בַּת.

verses.zh: 亚哈谢效法亚哈家行耶和华眼中看为恶的事，与亚哈家一样，因为他是亚哈家的女婿。
verses.en: He followed in the footsteps of Ahab’s dynasty and did evil in the sight of[NOTE:1] the Lord, as Ahab’s dynasty had done, for he was related to Ahab’s family.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in the eyes of.”

Heb “and he walked in the way of the house of Ahab and did evil in the eyes of the Lord like the house of Ahab, for he was a relative by marriage of the house of Ahab.” For this use of חֲתַן (khatan), normally “son-in-law,” see HALOT 365 s.v. חָתָן. Ahab was Ahaziah’s grandfather on his mother’s side.

verses.zh: 他与亚哈的儿子约兰同往基列的拉末去，与亚兰王哈薛争战。亚兰人打伤了约兰，
verses.en: He joined Ahab’s son Joram in a battle against King Hazael of Syria at Ramoth Gilead in which the Syrians defeated Joram.

verses.zh: 约兰王回到耶斯列，医治在拉末与亚兰王哈薛打仗的时候所受的伤。犹大王约兰的儿子亚哈谢因为亚哈的儿子约兰病了，就下到耶斯列看望他。
verses.en: King Joram returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds he received from the Syrians[NOTE:1] in Ramah when he fought against King Hazael of Syria. King Ahaziah son of Jehoram of Judah went down to visit[NOTE:2] Joram son of Ahab in Jezreel, for he was ill.
notes: Heb “which the Syrians inflicted [on] him.”
Heb “to see.”
